money_at_stake.basis: No dated source sizes the annual spend, capex, or revenue pool this specific occurrence moves. Three angles were searched and none clears the citation bar: (1) GAIA chip volume, pricing or revenue guidance -- TrendForce (2026-07-10, 2026-08-26) reports only that Samsung has handed prototypes to HP and Lenovo for validation, with mass production 'as early as 2027'; no unit, ASP, or revenue figure has been disclosed by Samsung or reported by trade press. (2) A PIM-specific market size -- the only figure found (a 'Processing in-Memory AI Chips' market report via openpr.com/Valuates Reports, USD 231M in 2025 to USD 44.3bn by 2032) is a template market-research-mill number with no visible methodology or primary data behind it, which is exactly the kind of number section 0.2 says reads as rigor and is not; it is not used. (3) Memory test equipment or EDA/compiler tooling spend attributable to PIM specifically -- searches turned up only academic literature (arXiv: 'New Tools, Programming Models, and System Support for Processing-in-Memory Architectures', 2508.19868, and PIMCOMP, 2411.09159), no commercial EDA product or vendor spend figure tied to PIM exists yet. Broader category totals do exist and are credibly sourced (TrendForce, global memory market to USD 1.28 trillion by 2027, 2026-05-29; AI PC market variously sized at USD 70-90bn for 2025 by multiple research firms) but none of them is the pool this occurrence moves: PIM is one incremental feature inside one vendor's one chip family, not the whole memory or AI PC category, and attributing the category total to it would manufacture the precision the method forbids. The leg is NULL rather than reached-for.

public_reach.rationale: Genuinely mixed rather than clean pure-play or clean unlisted. The parent ecosystem is public-company-dominated: Samsung Electronics is the party productizing LPDDR5X-PIM and building GAIA, and its named validation customers are HP and Lenovo, both public companies, not private buyers or state entities. That alone would argue for a high score. Held down from the 85+ pure-play anchor because the specific un-crowded sub-link this candidate is betting on (memory test and characterization tooling, and a compiler or programming-model toolchain for the PIM execution model) currently has no identified commercial, let alone listed, vendor: search turned up only academic papers on PIM compilers and no EDA vendor product announcement. So the reachable-today set is the memory maker itself (already the crowded, previously-discovered HBM trade per SIG-20260828-01), and the differentiated layer this candidate argues is un-crowded is not yet occupied by any named public company at all, reachable or otherwise. Scored at 58: above the 40 anchor because the buyers and the productizing company are unambiguously public and non-sanctioned, below the 60 'clearly reachable, mixed' anchor because the one part of the thesis that is supposed to be new and investable has no listed name behind it yet.

capture_odds.rationale: Pre-commercial and unproven, which is the dominant fact for this leg. There is no signed supply agreement, no disclosed pricing, and the only named commercial relationship is prototype validation by two OEM customers (HP, Lenovo) who are themselves large negotiating counterparties, a dynamic that has historically compressed component-maker margin rather than protected it. Scored near, but below, the 40 'some specs, mostly price-taker' anchor: there is neither a shipped product nor a finalized specification to anchor pricing power to yet, only a prototype in performance validation and a mass-production date attributed to unnamed sources (TrendForce citing ZDNet) rather than company guidance or a signed contract. An earlier version of this leg also cited JEDEC's April 2026 LPDDR6-PIM roadmap preview to argue that open standardization could invite qualification-gated competition from SK Hynix or Micron; that citation is dropped in this pass because businesswire.com and jedec.org both refused to load (timeout, then HTTP 403) and the Wayback Machine is unavailable in this session, so it could not be re-verified by fetch. The score is unchanged because the surviving TrendForce evidence alone already supports a sub-40 score.

timing_fit.rationale: Directionally inside the repo's 2 to 5 year horizon measured from the 2026-08-25 anchor, but on unnamed-source reporting rather than committed guidance. Two TrendForce reports six weeks apart (2026-07-10 and 2026-08-26) both point to the same target: mass production 'as early as 2027'. The second report's own body text only says 'next year' and attributes the timing to ZDNet reporting rather than to Samsung directly; the digit 2027 appears on that page's own headline, not stated as a digit anywhere in its body copy. Neither report is Samsung's own public guidance or a signed delivery schedule. Scored at 52, below the 60 'credible inside the window' anchor, because every date in evidence is a target attributed to unnamed secondary sourcing rather than a contract. An earlier version of this leg also cited JEDEC's unfinished LPDDR6-PIM standard as a further reason to score below 60; that citation is dropped in this pass because businesswire.com and jedec.org both refused to load (timeout, then HTTP 403) and the Wayback Machine is unavailable in this session, so it could not be re-verified by fetch. The score moved from 55 to 52 to reflect that only the reporting-quality argument now stands behind it, not the standard-finalization argument.

notes.text: UNRANKED is the honest result here, not a dismissal. Nell's own dimensions score this candidate on unmappedness and reach; what this appraisal adds is that nobody has yet published a number for what the occurrence moves financially, because the product has not shipped, the standard is not finished, and the 'un-crowded' toolchain layer she flags has no named commercial vendor at all today. Re-appraise on: GAIA volume or revenue guidance, LPDDR6-PIM standard finalization, or a credible primary-source PIM market-size estimate, whichever comes first.
